claims.statement: For every fixed eligible ordinary-tree instance (T,p) and its original strict favorable-leaf set F(T,p), the aggregate has the exact representation S(T,p)=sum_{B in I_(p+1)(T)} w_F(B)-sum_{A in I_p(T)} w_F(A), where w_F counts distinct original selected leaf tags. The finite bipartite one-vertex-deletion network with upper supplies w_F(B) and lower capacities w_F(A) admits a flow saturating every upper supply if and only if every deletion-neighborhood cut X satisfies sum_{B in X} w_F(B)<=sum_{A in N_-(X)}w_F(A); such a flow suffices to prove S(T,p)<=0. The full-upper-layer cut may be stronger than that scalar inequality because its neighborhood can omit lower sets. No universal validity of the cuts or sign is established.
claims.scope: The registered lower-region aggregate for finite ordinary trees with x(T)+2<=p and 3p<2alpha(T)+1, using the fixed strict original selector Delta_p(T-v)<0, original supports and neighborhoods, and separate multiplicity for every original leaf. The representation and finite flow/cut equivalence are per-instance statements only.
claims.reason: retained_narrowed: direct tagwise bijection verifies the fixed-selector weighted-layer identity, and integral max-flow/min-cut verifies the exact cut characterization for existence of a saturating flow. Such a flow suffices for the scalar sign, but the full-upper-layer cut sums only over its deletion neighborhood and is not automatically the scalar comparison over all lower sets. No universal cut proof or refutation is supplied; failure of a cut only obstructs this certificate.

limitations: No proof that the weighted deletion-neighborhood cuts hold for all eligible ordinary trees; the full-upper-layer cut can be stronger than the scalar inequality because its neighborhood may omit lower-layer sets.
No eligible instance with a failed cut, positive complete aggregate, or counterexample was produced; a proper-cut failure alone would refute only this flow certificate.
No computational replay was needed because the route makes an exact finite algebraic and network characterization rather than a census claim.
